NumPy array conversion¶

Design and public interfaces¶

Each material has a writable float64 structure of arrays, accessed through L.materials[p]. Materials share one grid. The coordinator deposits every material before combining periodic endpoints, identifying occupied nodes, and normalising mass-weighted fields.

The four neighbours are bottom-left, bottom-right, top-right, top-left. Particle and grid vectors retain three components; geometry and transport remain two dimensional. Constitutive tensor traces and norms reduce tensor axes only.

Particles(P, G, material, material_id) constructs one batch. ParticleSystem(P, G) coordinates the material list. Supported laws implement law(particles, material_parameters, simulation_parameters) and update history and dstress. The original five laws retain their existing Lie stress-rate integration; restored dp/dp_rate solids use a symmetric corotational spin split, and restored bingham/linear_mu fluids prescribe current stress directly. Rigid materials bypass the stress update and move at their prescribed velocities. See the constitutive audit for equations and integration tests. The registry in constit.py is the only material dispatch mechanism.

Uniform mass/volume properties, velocities, and grain fractions are copied into independent writable arrays. Initial velocity must be (3,) or (n, 3); composition must be (ns,) or (n, ns). Initial fractions must be nonnegative and sum to one. PHI, when provided, takes precedence over phi. Coordinates must have exactly n entries. Density, volume, and grain sizes must be positive and finite. A zero-particle material is valid.

The grid stores pressure, gammadot, mu, I, eta, and other constitutive diagnostics as mass-weighted sums. Call G.physical(name) to divide once by nodal mass. G.phi, G.s_bar, G.pk, and G.shear_rate are already physical fields. G.shear_rate is the bulk velocity-gradient measure formerly written over the deposited gammadot field. Empty-node quotients contribute zero. G.segregation_m, G.segregation_phim, and G.segregation_phi hold the deformable transport inventory separately from rigid material. G.segregation_particle_dphi stages the bounded species-aware increments for the next composition update.

Periodic left/right grid endpoints duplicate one physical node. Sum unique columns (array.reshape(ny, nx, ...)[:, :-1]) when measuring periodic totals. Merge deposited sums once per stage; do not add periodic endpoints a second time. Particle positions wrap with modulo arithmetic before cell lookup.

Timestep and compatibility¶

The supported timestep keeps the existing strain-before-force order:

  1. Reset grid, update loading, determine cells and basis functions.

  2. Deposit mass, momentum, composition, and kinetic pressure across all materials.

  3. Merge periodic sums, calculate valid nodes, and impose momentum constraints.

  4. Gather velocity, update strain/history/stress, and deposit diagnostics.

  5. Deposit forces, impose force boundaries, and update grid momentum.

  6. Calculate bulk shear rate and, if enabled, conservative segregation exchanges.

  7. Return species-aware composition exchanges, then update particle position and velocity and handle particle boundaries.

Mass and volume remain fixed during deformable motion. Reconstructed density is a diagnostic retained from the scalar solver, including its use in the existing Pouliquen low-density cutoff. This conversion introduces no density evolution law.

The following input conventions remain supported:

  • A single material object or list in P.S.

  • segregate_grid as an alias for segregate; contradictory explicit values fail.

  • Uniform initial_v, or per-particle initial velocities.

  • Existing pressure initialisation modes, steady viscous/Pouliquen flow, and the existing steady Poiseuille formula within its steady regime.

  • Boundary flags, default output flags, output filenames, and particle-data column order (x, y, grain fractions).

  • Legacy inlet placement and cadence. Only materials declaring inlet_rate enter through an enabled inlet. Injection properties must be uniform per material; each new batch gets freshly initialised constitutive history.

Outlets remove all persistent fields together. Inlets append full batches. Scratch connectivity is rebuilt after either operation, and material counts follow the actual array lengths. Prescribed per-particle rigid velocities travel with their rows through removal.

Callbacks are at_start(L, P, G), after_every_timestep(L, P, G), after_every_savetime(L, P, G), and at_end(L, P, G). The old after_ever_timestep spelling remains an alias. A custom callback replaces the corresponding default stage; it is responsible for any desired plotting, energy recording, or saving at that stage. Default energy histories grow with actual steps, so dynamic timesteps do not overflow preallocated buffers.

run lands on the requested final time without the legacy extra timestep. Dynamic timestep selection considers all materials and ignores inactive zero-speed or zero-segregation-rate limits. Invalid resulting timesteps fail explicitly. run(..., output=False) suppresses every output callback.

Intentional numerical corrections¶

  • Repeated node indices accumulate with bincount; advanced-indexed += no longer drops particle contributions.

  • Velocity gradient and transpose are no longer the same incremented buffer. Analytical rotation and nonsymmetric affine-flow tests cover this inherited bug.

  • Internal forces retain the spatial component in the stress-gradient contraction.

  • Cell lookup uses floor, validates the domain before indexing, and handles exact upper edges using the final cell. Periodic wrapping handles multiple crossings.

  • Grid validity is computed after periodic merging and all material deposits.

  • Segregation gathers use particle connectivity rather than particle masks as grid indices. Padding follows spatial rows and derivatives exclude the grain axis.

  • Closed-boundary/periodic KT ghost handling uses consistent spatial orientation; periodic endpoint duplicates are not treated as extra cells.

  • Shear rate, weighted diagnostics, and physical fields are distinguished so no field is overwritten or divided by nodal mass twice.

  • Friction uses actual boundary masks without modifying them. Rectangular-box indexing and the bottom silo mask no longer affect unintended rows.

  • At zero pressure, inertial number is undefined. Its stored diagnostic is zero; friction uses the infinite-inertial-number limit for nonzero strain rate. At zero strain rate with nonzero pressure, viscosity uses the existing cap. This avoids overflowing nodal sums with a machine-maximum diagnostic sentinel.

  • At exactly zero inertial number, the existing nonfinite-diffusion/zero-flux limit is explicit. Near-zero inertial number can still make the retained diffusion formula sensitive; it has not been regularised with a new physical parameter.

  • Gravity potential energy uses its Cartesian projection, avoiding division by a particle’s zero x-coordinate in the old angle-based expression.

The original five laws retain their constitutive equations, coefficients, tension convention, viscosity cap, and stress-rate formulation. The subsequently restored laws have explicit physical corrections and separate analytical tests; see the constitutive audit. The segregation flux, reconstruction, and return transfer were subsequently corrected to enforce mixture and species conservation; see the segregation correction. Changes are checked against analytical cases and independent corrected scalar kernels, not blind parity with known defects in master.

Runtime and dependency baseline¶

The supported baseline is Python 3.14, pinned to 3.14.10 in .python-version. Dependency floors are NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, Astropy 8.0.2, Matplotlib 3.11.2, and pytest 9.2. The complete resolved environment is recorded in uv.lock. Use uv sync --extra dev --locked with a current uv release to reproduce it. The Python 3.12.8 performance report is retained as a historical measurement; the full test suite is separately validated on Python 3.14.

Validation and remaining limitations¶

Tests cover shape functions, affine flow, pure rotation, repeated-node transfers, unequal particle properties, body/internal forces, constitutive histories, pressure and flow initialisation, multiple materials, empty batches, domain boundaries, periodic seams, inlets/outlets, dynamic timestep selection, callbacks, saved array shapes, and readable nonempty figures. The complete ball run and 100-/1,000-step bidisperse/three-class/eight-class segregation runs are included.

Kernel reference comparisons use rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12; short trajectories use rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-12. Tests run with runtime warnings treated as errors.

The corrected segregation operator conserves participating species masses and particle fraction sums to roundoff. A common slope limiter and numerical speed preserve mixture closure; physical diffusion is a separate flux. Nodal updates use species mass and the actual nodal control volumes. The particle return transfer exchanges equal mass locally and limits outgoing inventories before updating fractions, including across both spatial directions. Pure layers mix without freezing or acquiring negative fractions.

The reproducible before/after reports are benchmarks/segregation_drift_before.json and benchmarks/segregation_drift.json. They include 100- and 1,000-step runs with normalisation disabled. The explicit legacy normalise_phi option remains for compatibility and is unnecessary for the corrected operator. It should not be used to hide conservation errors. The old performance report predates this numerical correction; current small-case timings are recorded separately in benchmarks/segregation_correction_performance.json.

Retired implementations remain archived outside the active registry, with explicit retirement reasons. Absent laws remain unsupported. Mixed materials share the existing momentum grid; this work adds neither contact resolution nor a separate velocity field per material. Legacy traction scaling still uses the first material’s uniform reference density.

The user manual builds the current reStructuredText and Markdown sources together. See documentation maintenance for build instructions and the checked-in HTML layout.
